title: Could the unsolved text be another language? Eight aligned translations
question: Which of eight languages best matches the unsolved text under word-length and fixed-substitution assumptions?
summary: Eight aligned FLORES translations compared under explicit symbol and boundary assumptions. English is closest by word lengths; repetition statistics do not fit a single fixed-substitution explanation.

scope.representation: Existing rune-only joined LP2-00–55 token ledger, 2896 tokens, headings included; no decimal tokens. Three shared representations plus a Welsh digraph sensitivity; details in plan.
scope.procedure: Total variation distance between word-length histograms, bins 1..15 and16+. Lower is closer. Rank eight languages separately for each of first three representations. Never combine metrics into a language probability. IoC and within-word adjacent-identical fraction; separate distances under fixed bijective substitution only. Distinct symbol inventory reported. Dev language profiles classify each whole devtest language by word-length distance (8 held-out documents per representation). No tuning after scoring.
scope.parameters: Eight fixed languages; all 997 dev and 1012 devtest aligned sentences; 281 devtest article clusters; 200 paired bootstrap draws; seed 3301; 16 length bins.
scope.exclusions: No decryption; no claim one global cipher/language; no posterior; no all-language coverage; no genre-matched medieval/philosophical corpus; no unknown phonetic conversion; no unspaced languages or mixed plaintext inference.

finding: English has the smallest word-length distance in all three representations and all 200 paired article resamples. Other close candidates change order with representation. None of the eight letter profiles is close to the pooled rune IoC under a fixed substitution.
limitations: Similarity under assumed preserved boundaries and symbol units does not identify plaintext. Modern translated web prose differs in genre; GP grouping is only an orthographic sensitivity and can retain more than 29 symbols. Pages are pooled. Human review pending.
next_steps: A fixed genre-matched corpus remains open. Exact target-sized samples, known LP readings and aligned blocks are documented as related controls.

Shared-scale distributions for the manuscript target and all eight languages alphabetically. All languages use identical styling; 9+ is a display group, not the scoring bins.

reader_finding: English had the closest word-length pattern among the eight tested languages. It remained closest under all three counting methods.
reader_limit: This comparison assumes that encryption preserves word boundaries and word lengths. It ranks these reference texts; it does not identify the hidden language.
